payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source light-blue mug has been moved to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass only when the visual evidence establishes that the source mug is represented by an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates against the source mug's light-blue exterior, blue interior with a shadowed lower region, broad rounded body, rim and large curved left-facing handle. The edited right candidate has a dark interior, pale exterior, smaller tapered body and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a pale interior and a different appearance. Assess whether the combined features establish correspondence, not merely whether one candidate resembles the source more than the other. Interior darkness alone and right-side placement alone are insufficient. Allow for changed framing, lighting, relative scale and possible rotation; no individual difference automatically disproves identity. The distinct left mug matters only insofar as it helps establish where the source mug ended up: an unrelated extra mug is not itself a violation of this instruction. Treat the far-left blue blur as ambiguous unless recognizable mug structure establishes correspondence. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise was not moved to their right. Return unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position cannot be established; uncertainty about completion is not evidence of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflicts of the full comparison.
node.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale-interior mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of them. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess correspondence using the combined visible object features, then compare the corresponding mug's object-relative position with the edited headphones. Allow for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.

node_traces.evidence: The source mug is a broad light-blue mug with a large left-facing handle and blue interior. In the edited image, the mug to the right of the headphones has a pale exterior, dark interior, smaller tapered body, and right-facing handle; the mug left of the headphones has a pale interior and also differs in appearance. Neither edited candidate is established as the source mug by the combined visible features. The far-left blue blur is not recognizable enough to establish mug correspondence or position.

Do not turn the reference label “partial” into forced pass/fail or treat low confidence/variation as proof of missing progress. Keep correspondence and position as distinct checks, and calibrate uncertainty to the combined evidence.
